tool.name: KegAlign
tool.description: A Scalable GPU System for Pairwise Whole Genome Alignments based on LASTZ's seed-filter-extend paradigm
tool.command:
## Convert input sequences to 2bit -------------------------------------
## ⚠ NO PROCESS SUBSTITUTION HERE. `faToTwoBit <(gzip -cdfq ...)` is a bashism, and the ## job script is not guaranteed to run under bash: on usegalaxy.org's vgp destination the ## container's /bin/sh rejects it with `syntax error: unexpected "("` and the tool dies at ## exit 2 before reading a single base. The wrapper carried that line unchanged from ## 2024-08-29 and every container tolerated it until this one, so this is a latent bashism ## finally meeting a POSIX shell -- not a regression in the aligner. ## Decompressed to a real file rather than a FIFO or /dev/stdin so that nothing depends on ## faToTwoBit accepting a non-seekable input, and removed immediately after conversion so ## the uncompressed copies do not sit beside the 2bit files for the life of the job.
## ## ⛔ UNCONDITIONAL, AND MAKING IT COLLECTION-ONLY BROKE THE DEFAULT PATH. A previous revision ## gated this on `bundle_selector == "collection"`, on the belief that "run_kegalign converts both ## genomes AGAIN into its own $DATA_FOLDER". IT DOES NOT CONVERT ANYTHING. `data_folder` is an ## INPUT to the aligner -- src/main.cpp declares it "folder with sequence files in 2bit format" -- ## and the aligner only concatenates it into the lastz command strings it emits ## (src/segment_printer.cpp: `cfg.data_folder + "ref.2bit"`). It reads the FASTAs directly for its ## own work, which is why the alignment SUCCEEDS and only the packaging fails. ## ## MEASURED, EH23a x EH23b on vgp 2026-09-23: the GPU pipeline completed (11.6e9 seeds, 79.6e6 ## HSPs, 387 s) and package_output.py then died with ## missing source file .../working/work/ref.2bit ## because nothing on the tarball path had created it. The tarball MUST carry these: they are what ## the commands inside it reference, and batched_lastz runs those commands. ## ## ⚠ THE DISK SAVING WAS REAL BUT IT WAS NOT THESE FILES' TO GIVE. What is discarded on the tarball ## path is the two OUTPUT DATASETS, and `<filter>bundle_selector == "collection"</filter>` on ## target_2bit / query_2bit already prevents those. The files themselves are load-bearing on both ## paths. mkdir -p "\$(pwd)/work" && gzip -cdfq '$target' > "\$(pwd)/work/ref.fa" && faToTwoBit "\$(pwd)/work/ref.fa" "\$(pwd)/work/ref.2bit" && gzip -cdfq '$query' > "\$(pwd)/work/query.fa" && faToTwoBit "\$(pwd)/work/query.fa" "\$(pwd)/work/query.2bit" && rm -f "\$(pwd)/work/ref.fa" "\$(pwd)/work/query.fa" &&
## The scripts come from the kegalign package, which installs them to its bin ## directory alongside the aligner -- this tool no longer carries copies of them. ## `--tool_directory` still has to name that directory, because runner.py locates ## diagonal_partition.py through it and package_output.py locates lastz-cmd.ini. KEGALIGN_BIN=\$(dirname "\$(command -v runner.py)") && test -f "\$KEGALIGN_BIN/runner.py" &&
## Run KegAlign --------------------------------------------------------
## explicitly calling python to bypass a pulsar bug ## https://github.com/galaxyproject/pulsar/issues/341 python "\$KEGALIGN_BIN/runner.py" --output-type tarball ## ## ⚠ A LITERAL, NOT '$kegalign_output'. runner.py declares --output-file required, and then ## never reads it under --output-type tarball -- its tarball branch is `pass`, and the command ## file it does write is always `lastz-commands.txt`. Naming the dataset here was dead on BOTH ## paths, and on the collection path kegalign_output is filtered off entirely: Galaxy hands the ## template a NoneDataset "for tool writing convienence" (lib/galaxy/tools/evaluation.py), so it ## rendered as the literal string `None` rather than failing. Harmless today and a real pathname ## the moment --output-type stops being hardcoded. --output-file lastz-commands.txt --diagonal-partition --num-cpu \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-2} --tool_directory "\$KEGALIGN_BIN" '$target' '$query'
## Sequence Options ----------------------------------------------------
--strand '$sequence_options.strand_selector'
## Scoring Options -----------------------------------------------------
#set $scoring_pathname = str($scoring_options.scoring) #if $scoring_pathname != "None": --scoring '$scoring_pathname' #end if ## ⚠ THE REWARD/PENALTY PAIR LIVES INSIDE THE `ambiguous_params` CONDITIONAL, so the path carries ## that level too. Addressed one level too shallow, Cheetah fails only when a user picks something ## other than the default -- which short-circuits this whole block, so it never showed up. #if str($scoring_options.ambiguous_selector) != "x" #if str($scoring_options.ambiguous_params.set_ambiguous_params_selector) == "true" #set $argument_value = ','.join([str($scoring_options.ambiguous_selector), str($scoring_options.ambiguous_params.ambiguous_reward), str($scoring_options.ambiguous_params.ambiguous_penalty)]) --ambiguous '$argument_value' #else --ambiguous '$scoring_options.ambiguous_selector' #end if #end if
## Seeding Options -----------------------------------------------------
#if str($seeding_options.seed.seed_selector) == "custom" --seed '$seeding_options.seed.custom_seed' #else --seed '$seeding_options.seed.seed_selector' #end if --step '$seeding_options.step' #if str($seeding_options.notransition) == "true" --notransition #end if
## Ungapped Extension Options ------------------------------------------
--xdrop '$ungapped_extension_options.xdrop' --hspthresh '$ungapped_extension_options.hspthresh' #if str($ungapped_extension_options.noentropy) == "true" --noentropy #end if
## Gapped Extension Options --------------------------------------------
--ydrop '$gapped_extension_options.ydrop' #if str($gapped_extension_options.gappedthresh) != "" --gappedthresh '$gapped_extension_options.gappedthresh' #end if #if str($gapped_extension_options.notrivial) == "true" --notrivial #end if
## Interpolation Options -----------------------------------------------
#if int($interpolation_options.inner) > 0 --inner='$interpolation_options.inner' #end if
## Output Options ------------------------------------------------------
## Resolve the selector to the LASTZ format ONCE. It is needed twice -- here for lastz, and below ## for package_output.py, which records it in the tarball so batched_lastz can assign the Galaxy ## datatype. Passing the SELECTOR there instead of this value is what typed SAM output as `tabular`: ## batched_lastz's table is keyed on lastz format names, and `bam` is not one of them. #if str($output_options.format.format_selector) == "bam" #set $lastz_format = str($output_options.format.bam_options) #else if str($output_options.format.format_selector) == "general_def" #set $lastz_format = "general-" #else if str($output_options.format.format_selector) == "general_full" #set $lastz_format = "general-:%s" % str($output_options.format.fields) #else if str($output_options.format.format_selector) == "maf" #set $lastz_format = str($output_options.format.maf_type) #else if str($output_options.format.format_selector) == "axt" #set $lastz_format = str($output_options.format.axt_type) #else if str($output_options.format.format_selector) == "lav" #set $lastz_format = str($output_options.format.lav_type) #else if str($output_options.format.format_selector) == "blastn" #set $lastz_format = "BLASTN-" #else if str($output_options.format.format_selector) == "differences" #set $lastz_format = "differences" #end if --format '$lastz_format' ## todo :: rplot, bam ## --action:target=multiple ## $output_format.rplot ## .if str( $output_format.out.format ) == "bam": ## | samtools sort -@\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-2} -T "\${TMPDIR:-.}" -O bam -o '${output}' ## .else: ## > '${output}' ## .end if ## .if $output_format.rplot: ## && ## Rscript $r_plot > /dev/null 2>&1 ## .end if
## System Options ------------------------------------------------------
--wga_chunk_size '$system_options.wga_chunk_size' --lastz_interval_size '$system_options.lastz_interval_size' --seq_block_size '$system_options.seq_block_size' --num_gpu '$system_options.num_gpu' #if str($system_options.debug) == "true" --debug #end if
## Package Output ------------------------------------------------------
&& #if str($bundle_selector) == "collection" ## Growler: group the diagonal-partition splits into pair files -- one gzipped segments file per ## (target, query) chromosome pair, both strands, plus-before-minus as the lastz manual requires. ## No tarball, no commands.json, no format.txt: everything the grouping needs (target, query, ## strand) is in columns 1, 4 and 7 of the segment lines themselves. ## ## ⚠ `--format` above still selects what KegAlign writes into its command lines, but nothing ## reads them on this path -- the output format is chosen downstream, on Growler LASTZ. python "\$KEGALIGN_BIN/build_pairs.py" --segments-dir . --out pairs ## ## ⚠ THE QUERY 2BIT IS READ FOR ITS SEQUENCE ORDER ONLY, and it is already sitting in work/ at ## this point in the command. A batch holding several queries must list them in query-file order ## or lastz exits 1 with "segments must appear in the same order as the query file" -- measured, ## that rule is the one it enforces loudly. #if int($batch_lines) > 0 --batch-lines $batch_lines --query-2bit "\$(pwd)/work/query.2bit" #end if #else python "\$KEGALIGN_BIN/package_output.py" --tool_directory "\$KEGALIGN_BIN" --output_format '$lastz_format' #if str($system_options.debug) == "true" --debug #end if #end if

param.name: target
param.label: Target sequence file in FASTA format

param.name: query
param.label: Query sequence file in FASTA format

param.name: bundle_selector
param.label: Output shape
param.help: Tarball is the original two-step form, consumed by Batched LASTZ. Chromosome pairs emit one element per pair for Growler, which maps LASTZ over them without ever packing or unpacking an archive.
param.option: A collection of pair files, one per chromosome pair

param.name: batch_lines
param.label: Segment lines per element
param.help: Chromosome pairs only, and 0 turns it off. One element per chromosome pair makes the element count scale with the QUERY'S SEQUENCE COUNT -- fine for ten chromosomes, ruinous for a contig-level assembly, where a 300,000-contig query emits an element per contig per target. Above 0, whole query sequences are packed into elements of about this many segment lines, so the count is chosen rather than inherited. A single query is never split.

tool.help:
KegAlign is a scalable, GPU-accelerated system for computing pairwise WGA. KegAlign is based on the standard seed-filter-extend heuristic, in which the filtering stage dominates the runtime (e.g. 98% for human-mouse WGA), and is accelerated using GPU(s). KegAlign was designed as a faster replacement for lastz pairwise aligner.
**Using this tool**
.. class:: warningmark
This tool is the first part of a two-step process for generation of paiwrise alignments. The output of this tool is used as an input to **Batched LASTZ** tool. The *Batched LASTZ** can be found in the list of tool of this Galaxy instance.
**What it does**
KegAlign processes **Target** and **Query** sequences to identify highly similar regions where gapped extension will be performed to create actual alignments. The actual alignments are generated by **Batched LASTZ** that should be run on the output of this tool.
.. class:: infomark
Although this tool is only the first part of the alignment process all parameters related to generation of alignments are set **during this stage**.
**Scoring Options**
By default the HOXD70 substitution scores are used (from `Chiaromonte et al. 2002 <https://doi.org/10.1142/9789812799623_0012>`_)::
bad_score = X:-1000 # used for sub['X'][*] and sub[*]['X'] fill_score = -100 # used when sub[*][*] is not defined gap_open_penalty = 400 gap_extend_penalty = 30
A C G T A 91 -114 -31 -123 C -114 100 -125 -31 G -31 -125 100 -114 T -123 -31 -114 91
Matrix can be supplied as an input to **Read the substitution scores** parameter in *Scoring* section. Substitution matrix can be inferred from your data using another LASTZ-based tool (LASTZ_D: Infer substitution scores).
.. class:: infomark
From KegAlign 0.3.0, a supplied scoring file's ``bad_score`` and ``fill_score`` are honoured in the gap-free extension stage as well as the gapped one. Earlier versions read both values but used them only for gapped extension, so a custom file was interpreted two different ways within a single run. Results from a custom scoring file are therefore not directly comparable with those from 0.2.2.14 or earlier.
**Output Options**
.. class:: infomark
The final format in which alignmnets will be generated by **Batched LASTZ** are set here.
The default output is a MAF alignment file. Other formats can be configured in *Output Options* section. See LASTZ manual <https://lastz.github.io/lastz/#formats>`_ for description of possible formats.
